SMTO-SKL-0145 — Slack sent back more than SMTO can read at once

GUID: ec23c1f8-0181-5e5d-8687-0a394c6527ae
Slug: slack-result-limit-exceeded
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack's answer to this request was too large for SMTO to read in one go, so SMTO set it aside. This was a read, so nothing in Slack was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask for fewer items, for example the last 10 messages instead of a whole day, or one channel instead of all of them. A smaller request produces a smaller answer from Slack that fits SMTO's reading limit.
  2. Narrow a search with a person, a channel or a date, for example 'messages from Alex in #platform after 1 March'. A tighter search returns fewer, smaller results.
  3. If you need a lot of data, ask the Agent to go through it page by page and summarize as it goes. Reading in pages keeps each answer from Slack small enough to handle.

What success looks like

  • The Agent returns the Slack messages or items you asked for without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting what you asked for. Asking again for the same large request will hit the same limit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Slack Web API response exceeded the 2 MiB MAX_JSON_BYTES read limit and was discarded (for a write, this is reported as slack.mutation_outcome_unknown instead).

What this means

  • Slack API JSON streaming exceeds the two MiB bound; a mutation crossing this boundary is converted to unknown outcome. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack API JSON streaming exceeds the two MiB bound; a mutation crossing this boundary is converted to unknown outcome.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect response byte limit and operation effect classification.

How to fix it

  • Reduce the response size: use a smaller limit (history and thread return at most 15 messages per call), a narrower oldest/latest range, a specific channel or a more selective search query, and page through results with the returned continuation. Never treat a truncated response from a write as confirmation.
  • Narrow the request and use a bounded page. Do not treat a truncated provider response as a confirmed write.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A narrower read stays bounded; any affected mutation remains reconciled before repetition.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
